clue.text: Jno, a forester

definitions.meaning: Jno is the old written short form of John, so a little version of John
one of Robin Hood's outlaws living in Sherwood Forest

explanation.walkthrough: The first definition is a pun: 'Jno' is John cut down, a small John. Robin Hood's merry men were foresters of Sherwood, and his huge lieutenant bore this ironic name.
explanation.definitionFit: The abbreviation is a shrunken John, and Robin Hood's right-hand man was a famous outlaw of Sherwood Forest.

clue.text: 3's wife recorded finally in verse

indicators.note: the final letter sits inside the word for verse

parts.note: a lay is a narrative poem or song

indicators.note: finally takes the last letter of recorded

explanation.surface: The poet's wife is mentioned at the end of a poem.
explanation.walkthrough: 3 is the poet's answer at 3-down; his wife bore the title that matches his.
explanation.definitionFit: The spouse of a lord bears the matching title for a noblewoman.

clue.text: Of interest to those leading parties in Cumbria and Lancashire

indicators.note: the letters at the front of each following word, those that lead

explanation.surface: News relevant to people who head political parties in two northern counties.
explanation.walkthrough: 'those leading parties' looks like party leaders; 'those leading' takes the first letters of 'parties in Cumbria and Lancashire'.
explanation.definitionFit: A subject that is current and newsworthy is of interest right now.

clue.text: Organised London's entry as a writer

indicators.note: organised means arranged into a new order

parts.note: taken as written, S counted

explanation.surface: Someone arranged for an author to enter the capital.
explanation.walkthrough: The Victorian Poet Laureate is the writer.
explanation.definitionFit: The Victorian Poet Laureate was a celebrated poet and author.

clue.text: Those who wish to reach the other bank dry-shod must hurry

parts.words: Those who wish to reach the other bank dry-shod
parts.note: to cross a stream without wet feet you must leap across it, taken literally

explanation.walkthrough: The idiom for hurry is read literally as leaping across the water.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means get moving at once, act quickly.

clue.text: Jack, for instance, gets on in time

indicators.note: on is placed inside the unit of time

parts.note: an hour is a unit of time

explanation.walkthrough: In card games such as bridge, the jack, queen, king, ace and ten of trumps are the scoring cards so named.
explanation.definitionFit: In bridge the jack is one of the top scoring cards so named.

clue.text: Over the side

definitions.meaning: over in the sense of remaining or still there
one side of a thing, opposite the right

explanation.definitionFit: Something remaining is still there unused; one of the two sides is the port or sinistral side.

clue.text: Involve brother in tree-climbing

indicators.note: the brother goes inside the tree word
in a down clue climbing means read upwards, so backwards

parts.note: a lime is a tree, the linden

explanation.surface: A sibling gets drawn into climbing a tree.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'climbing' reads the tree upwards, so backwards; 'in' puts the brother inside that reversed word.
explanation.definitionFit: To drag someone into a quarrel or difficulty is to entangle them.

clue.text: You could thus baffle Houdini — but not for long

definitions.text: You could thus baffle Houdini — but not for long

parts.words: You could thus baffle Houdini — but not for long
parts.note: the famous escapologist slipped out of ropes, so binding him only puzzles him briefly; the phrase also means to confuse

explanation.definitionFit: To confuse someone utterly is the idiom; literally, tying an escapologist up only holds him briefly.

clue.text: Madman full of wine in carriage

indicators.note: the word for a madman holds the wine inside it, as a vessel full of drink

parts.note: dement is an old word for a lunatic
port is a fortified wine from Portugal

explanation.surface: A drunken lunatic sprawls in a horse-drawn coach.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Carriage' looks like a coach but means bearing or posture.
explanation.definitionFit: Carriage here is the way a person holds and moves the body, their posture or bearing.

clue.text: Round in 5? It can be played

indicators.note: the round letter is placed inside the honour's abbreviation

parts.note: clue 5's answer is an award; the OBE (Order of the British Empire) is one such
a round shape looks like the letter O

explanation.surface: A puzzle question about a round inside another clue, then a hint about something playable.
explanation.walkthrough: '5' points to clue 5, whose answer is an award; the British OBE is an example.
explanation.definitionFit: A woodwind instrument is something a musician plays.

clue.text: Wounded? This will buck you up

definitions.meaning: literally hit by a bullet in a limb
a boost or stimulus, figuratively an injection

explanation.definitionFit: Literally, hit by a bullet in a limb; figuratively an injection or stimulus that revives you.

clue.text: Tax small business in a small way

indicators.note: the business abbreviation goes inside the street abbreviation

parts.note: a way or street, written small as ST
a business or company, written small as CO

explanation.surface: A levy on a little firm, applied modestly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Small' twice means the word is abbreviated: CO for company, ST for street. The old tax survives in 'scot-free'.
explanation.definitionFit: An old levy or payment, surviving in the phrase scot-free.

clue.text: Try to get money from low land

parts.note: to touch someone is slang for asking them for a loan or cash
low, as in feeling low, is down

explanation.surface: Someone tries to extract cash from a stretch of flat country.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Try' looks like the rugby term, but it begins the slang for cadging money; the enumeration (5,4) shows a verb phrase.
explanation.definitionFit: An aircraft that comes to earth at the end of a flight makes contact with the runway.

clue.text: Bain-marie brings comfort to those retiring

definitions.meaning: a cooking vessel that keeps food hot
a lidded pan of coals once used to heat beds for people going to bed

explanation.walkthrough: 'Retiring' means going to bed, not leaving work.
explanation.definitionFit: A vessel that keeps food hot; and the long-handled pan of embers once slid between sheets to heat a bed.

clue.text: A low-lying island, in the main

definitions.text: A low-lying island, in the main

parts.words: A low-lying island, in the main
parts.note: main is the sea; low-lying is a pun on an island that lies beneath the ocean, the legendary sunken land

explanation.definitionFit: The legendary continent sank beneath the ocean, so it lies very low indeed in the sea.

clue.text: Hot? No! Let's get moving

indicators.note: the letters are set in motion and change places

parts.note: taken as written, with the S counted

explanation.surface: Someone refuses to stay in the heat and urges everyone to leave.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hot' is slang for stolen goods, not temperature.
explanation.definitionFit: Hot is slang for goods taken unlawfully, too risky to handle.

clue.text: Army nurse got sick in army boats

parts.note: Flo, short for Florence Nightingale, who nursed soldiers in the Crimea

indicators.note: sick goes inside the army abbreviation

parts.note: TA is the Territorial Army, Britain's reserve force
ill means sick

explanation.surface: A military nurse falls ill among the troops.
explanation.definitionFit: A small fleet is a group of ships or vessels.

clue.text: He suffers from the withdrawal of two forms of transport

indicators.note: withdrawal means drawing back, so the two transport words are read backwards

parts.note: RY is the abbreviation for railway
a tram is a street rail vehicle

explanation.surface: A commuter suffers when buses and trains are taken away.
explanation.walkthrough: 'withdrawal of' turns RY + TRAM backwards to give MART + YR.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who endures persecution or death for their beliefs suffers for them.

clue.text: Worried rough becomes rougher

indicators.note: rough treatment knocks these letters about

explanation.surface: An anxious, coarse person becomes coarser.
explanation.definitionFit: Noisier and more disorderly is the comparative of boisterous.

clue.text: Mournful-sounding architect?

definitions.meaning: jokingly, a gentleman who draws plans

explanation.walkthrough: The second definition is a pun: split as PLAN GENT, it is a man who produces plans, as an architect does.
explanation.definitionFit: A plaintive, resonant tone is mournful; and a designer of buildings is a fellow who makes plans.

clue.text: Cake's name concealed, but not in code

indicators.note: the name letter is concealed within the pastry

parts.note: an eclair is a cream-filled pastry

explanation.surface: A pastry's identity is hidden, though not encrypted.
explanation.walkthrough: The French phrase for a message sent in plain language rather than cipher.
explanation.definitionFit: The French phrase describes a message sent in plain language rather than cipher.

clue.text: Hear what goes into glass bottle

indicators.note: hear means take the sound of a word

parts.note: in glassmaking, metal is the molten glass itself

explanation.surface: Listen to what is poured into a glass bottle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bottle' is British slang for courage.
explanation.definitionFit: Bottle is British slang for courage or nerve.

clue.text: Sort of Western in which ponies can be seen

definitions.text: in which ponies can be seen

indicators.note: to sort letters is to arrange them afresh

explanation.walkthrough: 'Sort of' looks like 'kind of', but 'Sort' is the anagram signal and 'of' is fodder. The New Forest is a Hampshire woodland famous for its wild ponies.
explanation.definitionFit: Hampshire's ancient woodland is home to free-roaming native ponies.

clue.text: The horse to kick

definitions.meaning: a riding horse for hire or ordinary use
in football, to kick an opponent's shins

explanation.definitionFit: An everyday riding mount; and a foul in football, kicking an opponent's legs.

clue.text: Flatten a hill

definitions.meaning: a mountain or moor in northern England

explanation.definitionFit: To knock down a tree or opponent; and a northern English word for a moorland mountain.

clue.text: A good score is about one or two

indicators.note: the golf score goes round, about, the numeral

parts.note: par is a good score in golf
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A golfer's decent round is about one or two over.
explanation.definitionFit: A couple, a set of two matching things.

clue.text: Florentine, perhaps — a climber ate it moving around

indicators.note: the letters move around into a new order

parts.note: a liana is a tropical climbing vine

explanation.surface: A climbing plant devours something as it spreads.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Florentine' looks like the biscuit or a person, but it is an example of things in the style of Italy.
explanation.definitionFit: Something from Florence is an example of the style of Italy.

clue.text: Pattern or model — that covers it

definitions.text: Pattern or model — that covers it

indicators.note: the phrase before the dash covers, or holds within it, the letters wanted

explanation.surface: A dressmaker weighs up a pattern against a model and decides one choice will do for both.
explanation.walkthrough: 'that covers it' tells you the words before the dash hold the answer across 'Pattern or model', and those same words define it.
explanation.definitionFit: A standard or typical example serves as both a template and an exemplar.

clue.text: Vanessa a member of the Russian Navy?

parts.words: a member of the Russian Navy?
parts.note: jokingly, a Soviet, or red, naval officer of high rank

explanation.walkthrough: Vanessa is the genus of butterflies including this one; the rest reads it as a communist flag officer.
explanation.definitionFit: Vanessa is the genus of the familiar black, red and white butterfly.
